clue.text: Political party has to invite disdain

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a British political party
to invite trouble is to tempt it

explanation.surface: A political party courts public scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain and contempt are synonyms for scornful disregard.

clue.text: Man, learner in class

indicators.note: the learner's letter is placed inside the word for class

parts.note: a caste is a social class
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A man who is still learning sits within his social class.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess, the pieces are called men, and a rook is also known as a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess piece is a man, and the rook is commonly called a castle.

clue.text: Humming dreadful music? Order to be muffled

indicators.note: being muffled means wrapped up inside the other word, the noise around it

parts.note: noise is dreadful, unmusical sound
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone humming awful music is told to keep it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humming' looks like singing with closed lips, but here it is the slang sense of smelling bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Humming is British slang for stinking, and noisome means offensive in smell.

clue.text: See us sat about in one county or another

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit within the other county's name

parts.note: the clue's other county is Essex, neighbouring the east of London

indicators.note: about signals that these letters are moved around

explanation.surface: We sat about in some county or other, look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' jumbles US SAT inside ESSEX, a county north-east of London; the result is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: East Sussex is a real county in southern England, so it is one county.

clue.text: One hardly washing the back of the neck

definitions.meaning: an unkempt, grubby person, someone who seldom washes
the nape, as in held by the ... of the neck

explanation.definitionFit: A scruff is a scruffy person, and the scruff is also the nape of the neck.

clue.text: Country where hanging has helped elect president?

definitions.text: where hanging has helped elect president?
definitions.meaning: the 2000 US presidential election turned on partly punched ballot fragments, hanging bits of paper

explanation.definitionFit: Chad is an African nation, and hanging chads were the dangling ballot scraps in the Florida recount.

clue.text: Employ one for good in ugliest reshuffle

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges, here the letters of the word
one for good says the letter for good is replaced by the letter for one

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A government reshuffle puts one decent person in place of the ugliest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one for good' swaps the G of UGLIEST for I, giving ULIIEST, which 'reshuffle' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ something is to use it, and utilise is a synonym for use.

clue.text: Biathlon runner seeing the back of some Russians?

definitions.meaning: a biathlete ... cross-country, so a ... is the runner it glides on
many Russian and Polish surnames end in these three letters

explanation.definitionFit: A ski is the runner a biathlete travels on, and -ski ends surnames such as Tchaikovski.

clue.text: Times leader written into copy, which excites response

indicators.note: the leading letter is inserted into the word for copy

parts.note: a simulation is an imitation or copy

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The Times editorial was plagiarised, provoking a reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times leader' sounds like a newspaper editorial, but it is just the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimulation is something that excites a response, a rousing stimulus.

clue.text: How book reviewer might describe "The Cutest Dog the Vet Had Ever Seen"?

definitions.text: How book reviewer might describe "The Cutest Dog the Vet Had Ever Seen"?

parts.words: How book reviewer might describe "The Cutest Dog the Vet Had Ever Seen"?
parts.note: a gripping book is one a reader cannot set aside; a lovable dog is one no vet could bear to euthanise

explanation.definitionFit: A gripping book is called unputdownable, and the dog is too lovable for a vet to put down.

clue.text: Hurry to make appearance before waste collector

indicators.note: the appearance word comes before the collector word

parts.note: looks are one's appearance
a nappy (a diaper, in American English) collects a baby's waste

explanation.surface: Get a move on to look presentable before the bin men arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waste collector' suggests a binman, but it is a NAPPY, British for diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To look snappy is a British idiom urging someone to hurry up.

clue.text: Great performer in bed (forget name)

indicators.note: forgetting the name means leaving its letter out

parts.note: a divan is a type of bed

explanation.surface: A star singer lies in bed, unable to recall a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a great performer.

clue.text: Wife despaired, being treated as common

indicators.note: being treated means worked on, so the letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A wife despaired at being treated as vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being treated' signals the anagram; 'common' here means widespread, not vulgar as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widespread is common, found over a large area.

clue.text: Tenant announcing a reduction in drugs

indicators.note: announcing means spoken out loud, the phrase heard rather than read

parts.note: ... is slang for the drug ecstasy, so a reduction is less of it

explanation.surface: A tenant declares that they are cutting down on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: E is common slang for ecstasy, so 'less E' is a reduction in drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds a property under a lease, which makes them a tenant.

clue.text: Control disconnecting explosive weapon

indicators.note: disconnecting splits the explosive apart so the other piece fits inside

parts.note: TNT is trinitrotoluene, a high explosive
to ride a horse is to control it

explanation.surface: Defusing a bomb by cutting the wires to make a weapon safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, and also a missile, so a weapon.

clue.text: Men put in plug to form type of lid

indicators.note: the men are put inside the plug

parts.note: a stop is a plug or stopper
a crew is a group of men working together

explanation.surface: Workmen put in a stopper to make a kind of lid.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw-top is a lid that twists onto a container's threaded neck.

clue.text: Intimate picture reveals miss wearing half a bra?

indicators.note: wearing means having the other piece inside, as clothing goes around a body

parts.note: a bra has two cups, so one is half of it
to lose something is to miss it

explanation.surface: A revealing photo shows a woman missing half her bra.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a photograph taken at short range, an intimate picture.

clue.text: Rude image is beneath old bishop

indicators.note: in a down clue the picture word goes below the other pieces

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
a scene is a picture or image

explanation.surface: A vulgar picture is unworthy of an old churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive and indecent, which is rude in the strong sense.

clue.text: Cat gut the cool alternative

indicators.note: an alternative form of the letters, so they are rearranged
to gut a word is to remove its insides, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cool alternative to catgut for string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gut' leaves TE from THE, and 'alternative' mixes TE with COOL.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Blank design or exhibit's framed

indicators.note: framed means held inside the surrounding words

explanation.surface: An exhibit of design is shown in a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: To blank someone is to ignore them, a snub.

clue.text: In speech, certain characters appear — calm

indicators.note: in speech means spoken out loud

parts.note: the letter E written in the plural, Es

explanation.surface: When talking, certain people appear calm.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to calm or soothe pain or worry.

clue.text: Child unconscious, which creates offence

parts.note: a kid is a child
someone napping is asleep, so unconscious

explanation.surface: A child, dozing, causes offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnapping, the abduction of a person, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Passageway avoiding a small piece of land

indicators.note: avoiding the a means it is left out of the passage word

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between seats

explanation.surface: Walking down a passageway, steering clear of a tiny plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Ultimately, cost just criminal

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, picking the last letter of cost

parts.note: just means fair, reasonable

explanation.surface: In the end, the cost was criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasonable acts are criminal, amounting to betrayal of the state.

clue.text: Trouble, in a fix

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or fix them

explanation.surface: Trouble, being in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, so trouble.

clue.text: Old copper kitchen utensil

definitions.meaning: an early policeman, named after Robert Peel who founded the force
a tool for removing skin from vegetables

explanation.definitionFit: Peeler is old slang for a British policeman, and it is also a vegetable-skinning tool.

clue.text: Late job suggesting this missed?

parts.note: the late are dead
a line, as in line of work, is a job

explanation.surface: A job delivered late suggests the cut-off time was missed.
explanation.definitionFit: A late job implies that the time limit set for it was not met.
